title: DOJ data analytics flag a $10.6 billion catheter billing scheme; CMS withholds $4.41 billion (Operation Gold Rush)
summary: DOJ's 2025 Health Care Fraud Takedown says its Data Analytics Team detected anomalous billing by a transnational organization and that HHS-OIG and CMS prevented all but $41 million of $4.45 billion...
account: The Department of Justice's press release of 30 June 2025 announcing the 2025 National Health Care Fraud Takedown (324 defendants, over $14.6 billion in intended loss) describes Operation Gold Rush, in which an organization allegedly used foreign straw owners to buy dozens of medical supply companies and submitted $10.6 billion in fraudulent Medicare claims for urinary catheters and other durable medical equipment using the stolen identities of over one million Americans. The release states that the Health Care Fraud Unit's Data Analytics Team and its partners detected the anomalous billing through proactive data analytics, that HHS-OIG and CMS prevented the organization from receiving all but approximately $41 million of the approximately $4.45 billion scheduled to be paid by Medicare, that HHS and CMS intend to return the $4.41 billion in escrow to the Medicare trust fund, and that Medicare supplemental insurers nonetheless paid approximately $900 million. Nineteen defendants were charged and twelve arrested, four of them in Estonia. The release says that the Data Analytics Team was established in 2018 and announces a Health Care Fraud Data Fusion Center to leverage cloud computing, artificial intelligence and advanced analytics; it does not say that AI or machine learning was used in the Gold Rush detection.
purpose: Detect, investigate and prosecute complex health care fraud schemes.
system: Health Care Fraud Unit Data Analytics Team proactive data analytics (technique unspecified); Health Care Fraud Data Fusion Center announced
developer: U.S. Department of Justice, Criminal Division Fraud Section, Health Care Fraud Unit Data Analytics Team
deployer: U.S. Department of Justice with HHS-OIG and CMS
domain: Health care fraud and public insurance
taxonomy_note: The release credits 'proactive data analytics', not AI or machine learning, for the detection; artificial intelligence appears only in the announced Fusion Center and, separately, in defendants' use of AI to fake beneficiary consent recordings. Included at the database owner's instruction with the AI role marked unassessed. The single source is a DOJ press release, not a court document.

ratings.reason: The release states that $4.41 billion scheduled to be paid by Medicare was held in escrow for return to the Medicare trust fund, while supplemental insurers still paid about $900 million.
CMS and HHS-OIG stopped payment of all but about $41 million of $4.45 billion in claims from the organization, per the release.
The release describes over one million stolen identities but documents no outcome for the individual beneficiaries.

ai_role.statement: The detection is attributed to the Data Analytics Team's proactive data analytics, with no statement that AI or machine learning was involved; the Fusion Center that will use artificial intelligence is announced as future work. Developer and deployer of the analytics are the same public body (DOJ's Health Care Fraud Unit), acting with HHS-OIG and CMS.
